DOUBT proc resolution: app/proc/REPROC.prc:1 and app/proc/TRANREPT.prc:1 both declare '//REPROC PROC'. EXEC PROC=REPROC with JCLLIB ORDER=('AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.PROC') resolves by member name, so I used app/proc/REPROC.prc (one step PRC001 EXEC PGM=IDCAMS, REPROC.prc:21). app/proc/TRANREPT.prc (steps STEP01R, STEP05R, STEP10R) is not called by any J2 job; it looks like the source of the inline steps in TRANREPT.jcl. If a checker expands the call from TRANREPT.prc instead, the expected step ids differ.

proc node: I emitted no node for proc:REPROC (only jobs and steps, per instructions). call edges from the three proc-call steps (PRTCATBL.STEP05R, TRANBKP.STEP05R, TRANREPT.STEP05R) point to proc:REPROC.
//JOBLIB JCLLIB ORDER=(...) at PRTCATBL.jcl:19, TRANBKP.jcl:19, TRANREPT.jcl:19 is a JCLLIB statement, not a step or DD. No node or edge for it.

Proc symbolic: &CNTLLIB=AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CNTL comes from the EXEC statement (PRTCATBL.jcl:29-30, TRANBKP.jcl:23-24, TRANREPT.jcl:23-24). The proc SYSIN DD (app/proc/REPROC.prc:27) is a DSN DD, not in-stream, so it gives step:*.PRC001 -> ds:AWS.M2.CARDDEMO.CNTL read (member REPROCT dropped). Proc FILEIN/FILEOUT (REPROC.prc:23,25, DSN=NULLFILE) are overridden by the job's PRC001.FILEIN/PRC001.FILEOUT DDs.

GDG generations (+1) are dropped from DSNs. TRANSACT.BKUP(+1) is written by PRC001 and read by the SORT step as the same base DSN. TRANSACT.DALY(+1) written by SORT in TRANREPT (TRANREPT.jcl:51) and read by CBTRN03C in the same job (TRANREPT.jcl:65), that read is a COBOL data edge and not emitted here.
